# Setup and Authentication   [Skip link to Setup and Authentication](https://developers.etrusted.com/docs/authentication\#setup-and-authentication)

> In order to authenticate you will need to create an [API Client](https://developers.etrusted.com/docs/generating-api-credentials).
>
> Your API credentials should include a `client_id` and a `client_secret`, with these credentials you should have access to the APIs.

## Authentication   [Skip link to Authentication](https://developers.etrusted.com/docs/authentication\#authentication)

**NOTE:** For a more detailed guide on the authentication process please visit the [authentication section of our API documentation](https://developers.etrusted.com/reference/authentication-2).

Below is an example showing how you would authenticate using CURL:

tab="sh"

```shell
curl --location --request POST 'https://login.etrusted.com/oauth/token' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode 'client_id={client_id}' \
--data-urlencode 'client_secret={client_secret}' \
--data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
--data-urlencode 'audience=https://api.etrusted.com'
```

**Also, it's best to keep your `{client_id}` and `{client_secret}` away from prying eyes by authenticating on the [server-side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Server-side).**

On a successful request, you get back a response payload similar to this:

JSON

```json
{
    "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCIgOiAiSldUIiwia2lkIiA6ICJTVHpnYzZfTEM3ZHVnZkNoZVpoUzQyd0dNWVAyM0lBTUdkWGUtWTJrb3ZjIn0..dUuy0RXZjk0jyXH7X23JtJiID4ZYafVm1FPdh0Pv9xZHeZLQ1wn3xApwYr04IEhSZzcLWuTL0sJRrvXza24o4N8RkolBbfBiX1Vf_Dsj5YWczlhjd5yOsq-puvFW94-1XtjmFIvWWOV2zEraLYHxSc6UFvK6oCv99MvZecz_M1Hjo5-jHpwLWqVoC0d0v9rUhYcFT1ggw6aScO18CFpodz2P3851sZJj71Ldq7uq25y0IrNLXUabIPPCWZo5Cgfs_6NVIBB1L3y0ris8tXy0oZkg3CrdJT4O0QjEAwgpFl3RNNwwyGO7s4GKZCXfhfeHXkhzV8O29yoks-N-u22ljg",
    "expires_in": 300,
    "refresh_expires_in": 0,
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "not-before-policy": 1642608920,
    "scope": "profile email"
}
```

In subsequent API calls, you need to include the `access_token` as a `bearer token` in the request header. For example, if you wanted to request the list of reviews it will look something like this:

Shell

```shell
curl --location --request GET 'https://api.etrusted.com/reviews' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'
```

## What next?   [Skip link to What next?](https://developers.etrusted.com/docs/authentication\#what-next)

Once you can generate the `access_token`, the [concepts](https://developers.etrusted.com/docs/channels-1) will be the next best place to visit. It is meant to provide a general overview of the APIs available.

You can also go ahead and [explore the API documentation](https://developers.etrusted.com/reference/getting-started-with-your-api-1) if you already have an idea in mind and just need the right call parameters!

To learn more about the key standards our authentication flow is based on check [OAuth's official site](https://oauth.net/2/) and [jwt.io](https://jwt.io/introduction/).
